status_summary: No executive order or form change adding a First Amendment assurance to SF-424 applications was found. Executive Order 14332 (Improving Oversight of Federal Grantmaking), signed 2025-08-07, mentions free speech once in its findings but does not name the First Amendment, SF-424 or applicant assurances; it directs OMB to streamline application requirements and revise the Uniform Guidance. On 2026-05-29 OMB published a proposed rule (91 FR 32198) restructuring 2 CFR part 200, which lists a section prohibiting discriminatory event services; a law-firm summary of 2026-07-08 describes that section as barring recipients from discriminating in event services based on the viewpoint or content of speech, a related but different instrument that was not final as of 2026-10-17. The proposal's preamble groups that section with others meant to keep award funds from unlawful discrimination or uses inconsistent with law and Executive Branch policy, and the portions of the proposal read contain no First Amendment, SF-424 or applicant-assurance language.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14332, Improving Oversight of Federal Grantmaking, was signed (published 2025-08-12, 2025-15344); it requires senior appointee review of funding announcements, directs OMB to streamline application requirements and revise the Uniform Guidance, and includes no First Amendment assurance.
OMB, with grantmaking agencies, published a proposed rule, Regulation for Federal Financial Assistance (91 FR 32198, docket OMB-2026-0034), with comments due 2026-07-13.

title: Executive order requiring SF-424 grant applications to assure First Amendment compliance
uncertainties: Searches run: one web search by the researcher (SF-424, First Amendment, assurances, OMB Uniform Guidance, executive order on grantmaking) plus Federal Register API queries; the reviewer ran no web search and queried the Federal Register API for the rule's title since 2026-06-01, which returned only regulatory agenda notices and no final rule. The OMB proposed rule page was truncated, so a speech assurance in unread text cannot be excluded; the description of the event-services section comes from a law-firm summary, which says OMB targeted an effective date of 2026-10-01. The SF-424 forms on grants.gov were not inspected. Department grant certifications on DEI are a different subject and were not counted. In the 2026-10-17 review the Federal Register API record for the proposal (91 FR 32198 to 32305, 108 pages, comments closed 2026-07-13, no effective date) was read, and the full-text XML, the HTML page and the GovInfo PDF were each retrieved only to about 126,500 characters, which covers the preamble but not the regulatory text of proposed 200.219; none of the text read mentions the First Amendment, SF-424 or applicant assurances, and the only speech reference is a footnote citing the executive order on restoring freedom of speech. A Federal Register API query for the rule title from 2026-08-01 returned only regulatory agenda notices, so no final rule had been published as of 2026-10-17 despite the 2026-10-01 target reported by the law-firm summary.
